deep.reconstruction:
Context: Riemann's 1857 Nachlass text 'Zwei allgemeine Lehrsätze über lineare Differentialgleichungen mit algebraischen Coefficienten' (printed in the Werke, 1876). An n-tuple ('System') y=(y_1..y_n) of many-valued functions has branch points a,b,...,g. A positive loop around a acts by a constant matrix A, so y -> A y. A 'Klasse' is the set of systems with the same monodromy matrices A,B,...,G.

Previous page: A = alpha * diag(lambda_1..lambda_n) * alpha^{-1}, with distinct lambda_i. Put z = alpha^{-1} y. Then z_i -> lambda_i z_i, and z_i = (x-a)^{mu_i} * h_i(x), where h_i is holomorphic and nonzero at a. Here mu_i ≡ log(lambda_i)/(2 pi i) mod Z.

This page, part 1 (local exponents, Q-symbol):
- The lambda_i are fixed by A. So for two systems of the same class the corresponding exponents mu_i differ only by integers.
- These exponents can distinguish or group the systems of a class.
- Once the exponents are known, it suffices to give alpha instead of A, because the mu_i mod Z recover the lambda_i.
- Riemann introduces the symbol Q( a b ... g ; (alpha) (beta) ... (theta) ; mu_1 nu_1 ... rho_1 ; ... ; mu_n nu_n ... rho_n | x ). He first wrote and crossed out a cramped version. This generalizes his 1857 P-function scheme to n×n monodromy and is an early 'Riemann scheme' with local exponents.
- Remark: exponents are lower bounds. A system can be viewed as a special case of a system with some or all exponents lowered (by integers).

Part 2 (Theorem: any n+1 systems y^{(0)},...,y^{(n)} of one class satisfy Σ_k a_k y_i^{(k)} = 0, i=1..n, with polynomial a_k).
(a) The linear system (2) is n equations in n+1 unknowns. By Cramer's rule, a_k is proportional to (±) the n×n minor D_k of the n×(n+1) matrix Y=[y_i^{(k)}] with column k deleted.
(b) Each column transforms as y^{(k)} -> A y^{(k)} around a. Hence D -> det(A)·D.
(c) D is not infinite of infinite order at a. So D(x-a)^{-c}, with e^{2 pi i c}=det A, is single-valued with a pole of finite order. Thus D expands in powers of (x-a) rising by 1 from some lowest exponent.
(d) [explicit step mine] Since y^{(k)} = alpha z^{(k)} for every k, the matrix is Y = alpha Z and D = det(alpha)·Σ± z_1^{(1)} z_2^{(2)} ... z_n^{(n)}.
(e) The term z_1^{(1)}...z_n^{(n)} equals (x-a)^{mu_1^{(1)}+...+mu_n^{(n)}} times a function that is finite and nonzero at a. So its lowest exponent is mu_1^{(1)}+...+mu_n^{(n)}. Permuting the upper indices gives the lowest exponents of the other terms.
(f) [remark mine] All these sums are congruent mod Z to Σ mu_i, consistent with det A = Π lambda_i.
(g) The lowest exponent of D is 'in general' equal to the minimum mu over the permutations, and never smaller, since cancellation can only raise it.

Next page continuation: D·Π(x-a)^{-mu}... is entire with polynomial growth, hence a polynomial. So the ratios of the a_k are polynomials times powers of (x-a),... that differ by integers, i.e. ratios of polynomials. Clearing denominators gives polynomial coefficients. Corollaries: an n-th order ODE with polynomial coefficients exists, and every system of the class is a rational-coefficient combination of y, y', ..., y^{(n-1)}.
errors: No mathematical errors. Step (g) is correctly hedged: the true order of D at a is >= min over permutations of Σ mu_i^{(sigma(i))}, with equality only generically (cancellation can raise it). Riemann says exactly this ('allgemein zu reden ... jedenfalls nicht kleiner').

Implicit assumptions are left unstated on this page: the n minors are not all identically zero (otherwise the relation is trivial), and the systems have no singularities beyond a..g. The diagonalizability assumption (distinct lambda) was made explicitly on the previous page.
Minor point: Cramer proportionality needs alternating signs (±D_k); Riemann says 'proportional' loosely.

results.what: Local exponents mu_i at each branch point, fixed mod Z by the eigenvalues of the local monodromy, used to classify systems of a class.
results.modern_name: Local exponents / characteristic exponents of a Fuchsian system
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (1857 P-function paper; this Nachlass text), Fuchs 1865-66

results.what: Generalized symbol Q(branch points; diagonalizing substitutions; exponent columns | x).
results.modern_name: Riemann scheme generalized to n-th order (P-symbol with monodromy data)

results.what: n+1 systems with the same monodromy are linearly dependent over polynomials. Proof via Cramer minors, which acquire the factor det(A), and lowest-exponent estimates.
results.modern_name: Rationality of the space of solutions with prescribed monodromy (a Riemann–Hilbert-type finiteness argument; Wronskian-like determinant estimate)

results.what: Order of the determinant at a is at least the minimum over permutations of the sums of exponents.
results.modern_name: Local exponent of a determinant/Wronskian (precursor of the Fuchs relation)

deep.surprise_reason: This page is the draft of Riemann's well-known Nachlass paper 'Zwei allgemeine Lehrsätze über lineare Differentialgleichungen mit algebraischen Coefficienten' (1857, printed in the Werke 1876). Its content (Q-symbol, linear dependence of n+1 systems via determinants) is already attributed to Riemann. Only minor draft details, such as the crossed-out first version of the symbol, are new.

checkable.sympy: A=Matrix(2,2,symbols('a11 a12 a21 a22')); Y=Matrix(2,2,symbols('y11 y12 y21 y22')); simplify((A*Y).det()-A.det()*Y.det())==0
checkable.asserts: A minor of the transformed columns acquires the factor det(A) (step b).

checkable.sympy: Y=Matrix(2,3,symbols('y0:6')); D=[Y[:, [j for j in range(3) if j!=k]].det()*(-1)**k for k in range(3)]; simplify(Y*Matrix(D))==zeros(2,1)
checkable.asserts: Signed Cramer minors give the coefficients a_k solving system (2).

checkable.sympy: x=symbols('x',positive=True); m1,m2,p1,p2=Rational(1,3),Rational(1,2),Rational(4,3),Rational(-1,2); Z=Matrix([[x**m1*(1+x), x**p1*(2+x)],[x**m2*(1-x), x**p2*(3+x**2)]]); d=simplify(Z.det()); limit(d/x**min(m1+p2,p1+m2),x,0)
checkable.asserts: The order of det Z at 0 equals the minimum over permutations of the exponent sums (here min(1/3-1/2, 4/3+1/2) = -1/6); the limit is finite and nonzero.
Cancellation case: the actual order (11/6) exceeds the permutation minimum (5/6), so the bound is 'not smaller', with equality only generically.

transcription_corrections: After 'multiplicirt in eine Function die für x = a' the manuscript appears to read 'endlich und von 0 verschiedenen Werth hat' (an inserted word above, then a struck word after 'von 0'). The meaning is 'finite and nonzero'; '{+nicht+} unendlich' is equivalent in sense, but the inserted word may be 'nicht' or 'endlich'.
The struck word before 'Grössen' in 'die entsprechenden ... Grössen' is illegible, possibly 'Werthe'.
In the formulas, the upper indices on the mu's are system indices (mu_1^{(1)}, mu_2^{(2)}, ...), matching the y_i^{(k)} notation; the transcription renders this correctly.
